==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*lewh₁-}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:loos>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|loos}}, {{m|enm|los}}, {{m|enm|lous}}, from {{der|en|non|lauss|}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lausaz}}, whence also {{m|en|-less}}, {{m|en|leasing}}; from {{der|en|ine-pro|*lewh₁-||to untie, set free, separate}}, whence also {{m|en|lyo-}}, {{m|en|-lysis}}, via Ancient Greek. ====Pronunciation==== * {{enPR|lo͞os}} * {{IPA|en|/luːs/|a=RP,Wales}} * {{IPA|en|/lʉws/|a=SSB}} * {{IPA|en|/lus/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-loose.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/lʉːs/|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/lʉs/|a=Scotland,Northern Ireland}} * {{rhymes|en|uːs|s=1}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To let loose, to free from restraints. #* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|21|2|passage=Ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her; '''loose''' them, and bring them unto me.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1828|author=Thomas Keightley|authorlink=Thomas Keightley|title=The Fairy Mythology|volume=I|location=London|publisher=William Harrison Ainsworth|page=167|passage=And it was Thora, the little Dwarf's wife,
The five rune-books she took out;
So she '''loosed''' him fully out of the runes,
Her daughter had bound him about.}} #* {{RQ:Haggard She|passage="Ay, and one was nigh to being slain by the hot-pot to be eaten of those brutes, thy children, and had not the others fought gallantly they too had been slain, and not even I could have called back the life which had been '''loosed''' from the body."}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[unfasten]], to [[loosen]]. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To make less tight, to [[loosen]]. # {{lb|en|intransitive}} Of a grip or hold, to [[let go]]. # {{lb|en|archery}} To [[shoot]] (an arrow). # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[set sail]]. #* {{RQ:KJV|Acts|13|13||Now when Paul and his company '''loosed''' from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departing from them returned to Jerusalem.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[solve]]; to [[interpret]]. #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|5|11|passage=he had red her riddle, which no wight
